book_title:
The Epistle of Paul
to the Colossians.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF THE EPISTLE OF S. PAUL TO THE COLOSSIANS.
intros.text:
THE Epistle to the Colossians is not only in sense, but almost in words also, all one with the Epistle to the Ephesians, and was sent also by the same messenger Tychicus. c. 4. v. 7. And in it he maketh like mention of his bands and sufferings. c. 1. v. 24. and c. 4. v. 3, 18. And therefore no doubt it was written at Rome at the same time, to wit, in his last apprehension, yet before he knew of his martyrdom.
This difference there is, that he had himself preached to the Ephesians, but with the Colossians he had never been, as he signifieth c. 2. v. 1. Therefore although in matters of exhortation he be here briefer than to the Ephesians, yet in matters of doctrine he is longer. And generally he assureth them, that to be the truth, which their Apostle Epaphras had taught them, but namely he giveth them warning both of the Judaical False-apostles, who sought to corrupt them with some ceremonies of Moyses' law: and also of the Platonic Philosophers, who rejected Christ (who is indeed the head of the Church and the Mediator to bring us to God) and instead of him, brought in certain Angels as more excellent than he, whom they termed, Minores dij, teaching the people to sacrifice unto them (calling that, humility) that they might bring them to the great God. With which falsehood the heresy of Simon Magus a long time deceived many, as we read in Epiph. haer. 21.
Against such therefore S. Paul telleth the Colossians, that Christ is the Creator of all the Angels, God in person, the head of the Church, the principal in all respects: that he is the Redeemer, Mediator, and pacifier between God and men, and therefore by him we must go to God, so that whether we pray ourselves, or desire any other in earth or in heaven to pray for us, all must be done (as the Cath. Church in every Collect doth) Per Christum Dominum nostrum, that is, through Christ our Lord. or, per Do. nostrum Iesum Christum filium tuum, qui tecum vivit & regnat, &c. Whereby the Church professeth continually against such seductions, both the Mediatorship, and the Godhead of Christ.

verses.text: <sc>PAVL</sc> an Apostle of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ by the vvil of God, and brother Timothee:
to them that are at Colossa sainctes and faithful brethren in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ. Vve giue thankes to God and the Father of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ alvvaies for you, praying:
hearing your faith in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, and the loue vvhich you haue tovvard al the sainctes,
for the hope that is laid vp for you in heauen, vvhich you haue heard in the vvord of the truth of the Gospel,
that is come to you, as also <na>[1]</na> in the vvhole vvorld it is, and fructifieth and grovveth, euen as in you, since that day that you heard & knevv the grace of God in truth,

notes.text: He sheweth that the Churche and Christes Gospel should daily grovv and be spred at length through the vvhole vvorld. Vvhich can not stand vvith the heretikes opinion of the decay thereof so quickly after Christes time, nor agree by any meanes to their obscure Conuenticles. See S. Augustine ep. 80. in fine.

verses.text: as you learned of Epaphras our deerest fellovv-seruant, vvho is a faithful minister of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ for you,
vvho also hath manifested to vs your loue in spirit.

Therfore <na>[1]</na> vve also from the day that vve heard it, cease not praying for you and desiring, that you may be filled vvith the knovvledge of his vvil, in al vvisedom, and spiritual vnderstanding:

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 24 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: that you may vvalke <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> vvorthie of God, in al things pleasing: Fructifying in <na>[3]</na> cal good vvorke, & increasing in the knovvledge of God:

notes.text: So S. Ambr. & the Gr. Doctors, or thus: vvorthily, pleasing God &c.
c ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου
Many things requisite, and diuers things acceptable to God beside faith.

verses.text: in al povver strengthened according to the might of his glorie, in al patience and longanimitie vvith ioy
giuing thankes to God and the Father, vvho hath made vs <na>[1]</na> vvorthy vnto the part of the lot of the sainctes in the light:

notes.text: Vve are not onely by acceptation or imputation partakers of Christes benefites, but are by his grace made vvorthie thereof, and deserue our saluation condignely.

verses.text: vvho hath deliuered vs from the povver of darkenes, and hath translated vs into the kingdom of the sonne of his loue,
in vvhom vve haue redemption, the remission of sinnes: ⊢
vvho is the <cr>[1]</cr> image of the inuisible God, the first-borne of al creature:

because <cr>[1]</cr> in him vvere created al things in heauen, and in earth, visible, and inuisible, vvhether Thrones, or Dominations, or Principalities, or Potestates: al by him, & in him vvere created:
and he is before al, and al consist in him.
And he is the head of the body, the <sc>CHVRCH</sc>, vvho is the beginning, first-borne of the dead: that he may be in al things holding the primacie:
because in him it hath vvel pleased, al fulnes to inhabite:
and by him to reconcile al things vnto him self, pacifying by the bloud of his crosse, vvhether the things in earth, or the things that are in heauen.
And you, vvhereas you vvere sometime alienated and enemies in sense, in euil vvorkes:
yet novv he hath reconciled in the body of his flesh by death, to present you holy & immaculate, and blameles before him:

if yet ye continue in the faith, grounded and stable, and vnmoueable from the hope of the Gospel vvhich you haue heard, vvhich is preached among al creatures that are vnder heauen, vvhereof I Paul am made a minister.
Vvho novv reioyce in suffering for you, and do accomplish those things that vvant of the passions of Christ, in my flesh for his body, vvhich is the <sc>CHVRCH</sc>:
vvhereof I am made a minister according to the dispensation of God, vvhich is giuen me tovvard you, that I may fulfil the vvord of God,
the mysterie that hath been hidden from vvorldes and generations, but novv is manifested to his sainctes,
to vvhom God vvould make knovven the riches of the glorie of this sacrament in the Gentiles, vvhich is Christ, in you the hope of glorie,
vvhom vve preache, admonishing euery man, and teaching euery man in al vvisedom, that vve may present euery man perfect in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
Vvherein also I labour striuing according to his operation vvhich he vvorketh in me in povver.

chapters.summary: Saying, that he thanketh God for their excellent faith and charitie, and continually praieth for their encrease, he doeth vvithal giue vvitnes to the preaching of their Apostle Epaphras, and extolleth the grace of God in bringing them to Christ, vvho is cheefe aboue al, and peacemaker by his bloud. This is the Gospel vvas not of Epaphras alone, but of the vniuersal Church, and of Paul him self vvho also suffereth for it.

verses.text: <sc>FOR</sc> I vvil haue you knovv brethren, vvhat maner of care I haue for you and for them that are at Laodicia, and vvhosoeuer haue not seen my face in the flesh:
that their hartes may be comforted, instructed in charitie, & vnto al the riches of the fulnes of vnderstanding, vnto the knovvledge of the mysterie of God the Father of Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>,
in vvhom be al the treasures of vvisedom and knovvledge hidde.
But this I say <na>[1]</na> that no man deceiue you in loftines of vvordes.

notes.text: Heretikes do most commonly deceiue the people vvith eloquēce namely such as haue it by the gift of nature, as the Heretikes of al ages had, & lightly al seditious persons, vvhich dravv the vulgar sort to sedition by the allurement of their tongue. Nothing (saith S. Hierom. ep. 2. ad Nepotian.) is so easie as vvith volubilitie of tongue to deceiue the vnlearned multitude, vvhich vvhatsoeuer it vnderstandeth not, doth the more admire and vvonder at the same. The Apostle here calleth it, πιθανολογίαν, persuasible speache.

verses.text: For although I be absent in body, yet in spirit I am vvith you: reioycing, & seeing your order, & the constancie of that your faith vvhich is in Christ.
Therfore as you haue receiued <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ our Lord, vvalke in him,
rooted and built in him, and confirmed in the faith, as also you haue learned, abounding <na>[1]</na> <alt>`in him</alt>' in thankes-giuing.

notes.text: `in it

verses.text: Bevvare lest any man deceiue you by philosophie, and vaine fallacie: according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the vvorld, and not according to Christ.
For in him dvvelleth al the fulnesse of the Godhead corporally:
and you are in him replenished, vvho is the head in al Principalitie and Povver:
in vvhom al you are circumcised vvith circumcision not made by hand in spoiling of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,
buried vvith him in Baptisme: in vvhom also you are risen againe by the faith of the operation of God, vvho raised him vp from the dead.
And you <cr>[1]</cr> vvhen you vvere dead in the offenses and the prepuce of your flesh, did he quicken together vvith him: pardoning you al offenses,
vvyping out the hand vvriting <na>[1]</na> <alt>`of decree</alt>' that vvas against vs, vvhich vvas contrarie to vs. and the same he hath taken out of the vvay, fastening it to the crosse:

notes.text: `by decrees

verses.text: and spoiling the Principalities and Potestats, <na>[1]</na> hath ledde them confidently in open shevv, triumphing them in him self.

notes.text: That is, vvilful or selfwilled in voluntarie religiō. for that is, θέλων ἐν θρησκείᾳ, vvhereof commeth the vvord folovving ἐθελοθρησκεία, Superstitiō. v. 23. See Annot. v. 21.

verses.text: Let no man therfore iudge you in meate or in drinke, or in part of a festiual day, or of the Nevv-moone, or of Sabboths:
vvhich are a shadovv of things to come, but the body Christs.
Let no man seduce you, <na>[1]</na> bvvilling in the humilitie and religion of Angels, vvalking in the things vvhich he hath not seen, in vaine puffed vp by the sense of his flesh,

notes.text: c ἐδειγμάτισεν.

verses.text: and not holding the head, vvhereof the vvhole body by ioyntes and bandes being <na>[1]</na> serued & compacted, grovveth to the increase of God.

notes.text: ἐπιχορηγούμενον. That is, taking subministration of spiritual life and nourishment by grace from Christ the head.

verses.text: If then you be dead vvith Christ, from the elements of this vvorld: vvhy do you yet <na>[1]</na> decree as liuing in the vvorld?

notes.text: c δογματίζεσθε

verses.text: Touch not, tast not, handle not:
vvhich things are al vnto destruction by the very vse, according to the precepts and doctrines of men.
vvhich are in deede hauing a shevv of vvisedom in superstition and humilitie, and not to spare the body, not in any honour to the filling of the flesh.

chapters.summary: He is careful for them, though he vvere neuer vvith them: that they rest in the vvonderful vvisedom vvhich is in Christian religion, and be not caried avvay either vvith Philosophie, to leaue Christ and to sacrifice to Angels: or vvith Iudaisme, to receiue any ceremonies of Moyses lavv.

verses.text: <sc>THERFORE</sc> <na>[1]</na> if you be risen vvith Christ, seeke the things that are aboue: vvhere Christ is sitting on the right hand of God.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon Easter eue.

verses.text: Minde the things that are aboue, not the things that are vpon the earth.
For you are dead: and your life is hidde vvith Christ in God.
Vvhen Christ shal appeare, your life: then you also shal appeare vvith him in glorie. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> Mortifie therfore your members that are vpon the earth, fornication, vncleannesse, lust, euil concupiscence, and auarice, vvhich is <na>[2]</na> the seruice of Idols.

notes.text: c ἐιδωλολατρεία.

verses.text: for vvhich things the vvrath of God commeth vpon the children of incredulitie.
in vvhich you also vvalked sometime, vvhen you liued in them.
But novv lay you also al avvay: anger, indignation, malice, blasphemie, filthie talke out of your mouth.
Lie not one to an other: <cr>[1]</cr> spoiling your selues of the old man vvith his actes,
and doing on the nevv, him that is renewed vnto knovvledge, <cr>[1]</cr> according to the image of him that created him.
vvhere there is not, Gentile and Ievve, circumcision and prepuce, Barbarous and Scythian. bonde and free: but al, and in al Christ.
<cr>[1]</cr> Put ye on therfore as the elect of God, holy, and beloued, <na>[2]</na> the bovvels of mercie, benignitie, humilitie, modestie, patience,

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 5 Sunday after the Epiphanie.

verses.text: supporting one an other: and pardoning one an other, if any haue a quarel against any man. as also our Lord hath pardoned vs: so you also.
But aboue al these things haue charitie, vvhich is the band of perfection:
& let the peace of Christ <na>[1]</na> cexult in your hartes, vvherein also you are called in one body: and be thankeful.

notes.text: βραβευέτω, triumph and haue the victorie.

verses.text: Let the vvord of Christ dvvel in you aboundantly, in al vvisedom: teaching and admonishing your ovvne selues, vvith psalmes, hymnes, and spiritual canticles, in grace singing in your hartes to God.
Al vvhatsoeuer you doe in vvord or in vvorke, al things in the name of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, giuing thankes to God and the Father by him. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> Vvomen be subiect to your husbands, as it behoueth in our Lord.
<cr>[1]</cr> Men, loue your vviues: and be not bitter tovvard them.
<cr>[1]</cr> Children obey your parents in al things: for that is vvel pleasing to our Lord.
Fathers, prouoke not your children to indignation: that they become not discouraged.
<cr>[1]</cr> Seruants, obey in al things, your maisters according to the flesh, not seruing to the eie, as pleasing men, but in simplicitie of hart, fearing God.
Vvhatsoeuer you doe, vvorke it from the hart as to our Lord, and not to men:
knovving that you shal receiue of our Lord the <na>[1]</na> retribution of inheritance. Serue our Lord Christ.

notes.text: Retribution or revvard for good vvorkes: ἀνταπόδοσις, vvhich signifieth rendering one for an other.

verses.text: For he that doeth iniurie, shal receiue that vvhich he hath done vniustly: and <cr>[1]</cr> there is not acception of persons vvith God.

chapters.summary: He exhorteth to mortifie and put of al corrupt maners of the old man, and to put on such vertues as are for the new man. 18 In particular also, vviues and husbands, children and parents, seruants and maisters, ech sort to do their duetie.

verses.text: <sc>YOV</sc> Maisters, that vvhich is iust and equal, doe to your seruants: knovving that you also haue a Maister in heauen.
<cr>[1]</cr> Be instant in praier: vvatching in it in thankes giuing,
<cr>[1]</cr> praying vvithal <na>[2]</na> for vs also, that God may open vnto vs the doore of speache to speake the mysterie of Christ ( for the vvhich also I am bound )

notes.text: 2. Thes. 3, 1. · S. Paul euer much desireth the praiers of the faithful: vvhereby vve learne the great efficacie of them.

verses.text: that I may manifest it, so as I ought to speake.
<cr>[1]</cr> Vvalke vvith vvisedom tovvard them that be vvithout: redeeming the time.
Your talke alvvaies, in grace let it be seasoned vvith salte: that you may knovv hovv you ought to ansvver euery man.
The things that are about me, Tychicus our deerest brother, and faithful minister, & fellovv-seruant in our Lord, vvil make you vnderstand al,
vvhom I haue sent to you for this same purpose, that he may know the things that concerne you, and may comfort your hartes,
vvith <cr>[1]</cr> Onesimus the most deere and faithful brother vvho is of you. Al things that are done here, shal they doe you to vnderstand.
Aristarchus my fellovv-prisoner saluteth you, & Marke the cosin-german of Barnabas ( concerning vvhom you haue receiued commaundements, If he come to you, receiue him )
and Iesus that is called Iustus: vvho are of the Circumcision. these only are my coadiutors in the kingdom of God: vvhich haue been a comfort to me.
Epaphras saluteth you vvho is of you, the seruant of Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, alvvaies careful for you in praiers, that you may stand perfect and ful in al the vvil of God.
For I giue him testimonie that he hath much <na>[1]</na> labour for you, and for them that be at Laodicia, and that are at Hierapolis.

notes.text: He did not only pray, but tooke other great paines to procure Gods grace for the Colossians : perhaps by vvatching, fasting, and doing other penance of body: that God vvould not suffer them to fall from their receiued faith to the secte of Simon Magus or the Iudaizing christians.

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> Luke the most deere physicion saluteth you: and Demas.
Salute the brethren that are at Laodicia: and Nymphas and the Church that is in his house.
And vvhen the epistle shal be read vvith you, make that it be read also in the Church of the Laodicians: and that you read that vvhich is of the Laodicians.
And say to Archippus, See the ministerie vvhich thou hast receiued of our Lord, that thou fulfil it.
The salutation: vvith mine ovvne hand, Paules. Be mindeful of my bandes. Grace be vvith you. Amen.

chapters.summary: He exhorteth to instance in praier, 5 and to vvisedom in behauiour. 7 He sendeth Tychicus. 10 He doeth commendations, 15 and inioyneth to be done.
